elements.quote: The primary outcomes of this systematic review are first pass ETI and overall ETI success. Secondary outcomes include time to ETI, ease-of-use and ETI complications such as oesophageal intubation.
elements.reason: Outcomes are listed but explicit definitions (e.g., criteria for success) are not provided.
No time frame of measurement for the outcomes is specified in the provided text.

elements.quote: We extracted the following data: (1) characteristics of included studies; (2) first pass ETI success and overall ETI success of included studies.
elements.reason: The text states what data was extracted but does not explicitly state whether all compatible results were sought.
There is no evidence that not all compatible results were sought; standard extraction is implied.
No evidence of changes to outcome-domain inclusion, definitions, or importance is reported.
No evidence of changes to processes for selecting results within eligible outcome domains is reported.

elements.quote: The primary outcomes of this systematic review are first pass ETI and overall ETI success... The aim of this study was to systematically review the literature relevant to the use of bougies and stylets for ETI in the prehospital setting. This should inform a conclusion regarding their prehospital efficacy and allow practitioners to decide whether and how best to incorporate these devices into their practice.
elements.reason: Primary outcomes are identified, and the rationale for the review's aim is provided, though specific prioritization rationale is implicit.

elements.quote: We extracted the following data: (1) characteristics of included studies; (2) first pass ETI success and overall ETI success of included studies.
elements.reason: Variables for data extraction are listed (e.g., study characteristics, success rates), but they are not explicitly defined (e.g., no definition of what constitutes 'first pass ETI success').
The manuscript does not describe any assumptions made about missing or unclear information during the data extraction process.
No tool used to determine which data items to collect is cited in the provided evidence.

elements.quote: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) quality assessment tool for observational cohort and cross-sectional studies was used independently by both reviewers (J.T., and Z.A.) to assess the methodological quality of included studies [12].
elements.reason: The specific tool name is provided, but a version number is not explicitly stated in the text.

elements.quote: This tool assessed 14 criteria including study objectives, population, sample, exposures, outcomes and analyses.
elements.reason: Examples of criteria are listed, but the complete list of all 14 domains/items is not specified.

elements.quote: Bonnette et al. [14] had the highest proportion (79%) of criteria answered 'yes' (i.e. high quality)
elements.reason: An overall judgement is inferred from the proportion of 'yes' answers, but explicit rules or thresholds for deriving this judgement are not fully detailed.
No adaptations to the tool were mentioned; the standard NIH tool appears to have been used without modification.
A newly developed tool was not used; an existing NIH tool was employed.

elements.quote: The National Institutes of Health (NIH) quality assessment tool for observational cohort and cross-sectional studies was used independently by both reviewers (J.T., and Z.A.) to assess the methodological quality of included studies [12]. ... Any discrepancies were resolved by discussion between the authors.
elements.reason: The number of reviewers (two), their independence, and the procedure for resolving disagreements (discussion) are clearly reported.
There is no description of processes used to obtain or confirm risk-of-bias information from study investigators.
There is no mention of automation tools being used for risk-of-bias assessment.

elements.quote: Dichotomous outcomes were analysed using risk ratios (RR) as summary statistics. The effect sizes were reported as weighted mean differences and the precision of effects sizes were reported at a confidence interval (CI) of 95%.
elements.reason: The Statistical Analysis section explicitly specifies the effect measures used for dichotomous outcomes (risk ratios) and other effect sizes (weighted mean differences).

The manuscript reports thresholds for statistical significance (p < 0.05) but does not report thresholds or ranges used to interpret the magnitude of the effect size (e.g., clinical significance of RR values).
There is no description of methods used to re-express synthesized results using another effect measure.

While the effect measures are specified, the manuscript does not provide a justification for why risk ratios or weighted mean differences were chosen over other potential measures (e.g., odds ratios).

elements.quote: Four studies [23-26] were included in our meta-analysis of a bougie versus non-bougie method overall ETI success for simulation studies without video technology (Fig. 5). The primary outcome of overall ETI success was chosen for this analysis as first pass ETI success was not fully reported in five of the simulation studies without video technology [17, 18, 23, 25, 26].
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the process for determining study eligibility for specific syntheses (meta-analyses), noting that studies were excluded from quantitative synthesis if outcome data (first pass ETI success) was not fully reported, while still being included in qualitative synthesis.

The manuscript describes the statistical models and software used for synthesis (text_8) and notes that some studies had missing data in the results (text_11), but it does not explicitly describe the methods used to prepare the data for synthesis, such as how missing summary statistics were handled or if data conversions were performed.

elements.quote: Table 4 summarises the primary outcomes of first pass ETI success and overall ETI success for studies with a simulation design without video technology [17, 18, 23-26].
elements.reason: The manuscript explicitly describes the content and purpose of the tables used to display results, including the specific outcomes summarized.

elements.quote: Fig. 3 Forest plot of comparison between bougie versus stylet; outcome, first pass success rate in studies without video technology
elements.reason: The manuscript describes the graphical methods used, specifically identifying forest plots and flowcharts used to display results.

elements.quote: Two studies [20, 21] were included in our meta-analysis of bougie versus stylet first pass ETI success for prehospital studies without video technology (Fig. 3)
elements.reason: The manuscript reports the basis for grouping studies within the tables and figures (e.g., by study design, technology type, and outcome).
The manuscript uses standard graphical methods (PRISMA flowcharts, quality assessment bar charts, and forest plots) and does not report using non-standard graphs.
